title: Plasma disruption prediction and mitigation
bottleneck: Tokamak plasmas can disrupt, losing confinement in milliseconds and dumping megajoules of energy into the walls while inducing massive electromagnetic forces on the vessel. In a power plant, even rare disruptions would damage first walls and blankets, and runaway electron beams generated during disruptions can drill holes in plasma-facing components. Prediction must work with near-perfect reliability because mitigation through massive gas injection must trigger within milliseconds.
why_it_blocks: A commercial reactor cannot tolerate unmitigated disruptions. Each one risks weeks of repair downtime and cumulative wall damage, so disruption control is a licensing and economic prerequisite, not a research nicety.
current_state: Machine-learning predictors on existing tokamaks reach high accuracy on historical data, and shattered-pellet injection is ITER's baseline mitigation. Whether these scale to burning plasmas with alpha-particle-driven instabilities is untested.

sources.title: Reliable Nuclear Fusion Will Require New Heat- and Radiation-Resilient Materials
